environment: Humpback whales wrap up their epic Queensland coast migration with another strong calf season
Bull sharks return to the Brisbane River as the spring warm up kicks the ecosystem into gear
science: Queensland researchers edge closer to heat tolerant coral that could help the reef ride out warmer summers
sports: Queensland cricket gears up for a new Sheffield Shield season with the Gabba being readied for summer
stories.overview: Spring sunshine floods the Sunshine State as community tree planting days draw bumper crowds across the southeast

segments.title: The Open
segments.script: Morning legends, you're locked onto ParkSyde Bright Side and its Thursday the first of October, which means spring is well and truly out of its pyjamas. Im Alex Mercer, feeling a bit chipper because the mozzies havent found me yet this season. And Im Jamie, buzzing because todays show is full of good stuff, whales, sharks, cricket and a weather pattern thats actually behaving itself for once. We've got a ripper of a lineup for you this morning. Too right. Grab your cuppa, settle in, and lets get into the good oil happening right across Queensland today.

segments.title: Green Desk
segments.script: First up, the humpbacks are putting on one last show as they finish their migration south past our coastline. Spotters up and down from the Gold Coast to Hervey Bay reckon its been a cracker season for mums and calves this year. Yeah, and closer to home the bull sharks are back cruising up the Brisbane River, which sounds terrifying but honestly its just a sign the river systems ticking along nicely as the water warms up. Scientists love seeing them turn up right on schedule. Its basically natures version of the swallows coming back to Capistrano, except with a lot more teeth. Either way, its a good reminder spring in Queensland means the whole ecosystem wakes up at once.

segments.title: Science & Tomorrow
segments.script: Now for the science desk, and researchers here in Queensland are chipping away at something pretty special, coral that can cope with hotter water without bleaching out. Its early days but the labs are buzzing about the potential for the reef long term. Its the kind of slow and steady science that doesnt always make headlines but could genuinely change the game for the Great Barrier Reef. Every bit of heat tolerance they can breed in gives the reef a bit more breathing room. Exactly, its not a silver bullet, but its a solid step in the right direction. Good on the boffins for sticking with it.

segments.title: Weather
segments.script: Cheers Alex, Sam here with your southeast Queensland outlook, and its shaping up as a classic spring week. Expect plenty of sunshine across Brisbane, the Gold Coast and Sunshine Coast today, with tops around the mid to high twenties and that lovely light sea breeze kicking in by the afternoon. We are keeping an eye on the ranges though, as the atmosphere is getting a bit twitchy out west, which is pretty typical as we head deeper into storm season. Nothing to worry about just yet, but its a timely reminder to dust off the storm kit before the afternoon build ups properly set in next month. Back to you two in the studio.

segments.title: The Scoreboard
segments.script: Sporting front now, and cricket fans can finally exhale because the new Sheffield Shield season is almost here. The Gabba groundstaff have been out there fussing over the pitch like its a prize winning garden bed. Love that for them. Theres always something about that first smell of cut grass and linseed oil that means summer sports season is officially open for business. Couldnt agree more, and with the Broncos and Maroons fans still riding high from the footy finals, Queenslanders have plenty to cheer about heading into the warmer months.

segments.title: Overview & Outro
segments.script: Well thats a wrap for todays Bright Side, and honestly what a cracking bunch of stories. Whales, sharks, cricket pitches and hopeful coral, Queensland is pulling out all stops this spring. It really is, and that overview story about the tree planting crowds just tops it off beautifully. Theres something lovely about seeing whole communities out there with a shovel on a Thursday. Gives you a bit of hope for the place, doesnt it. Right, thats us done and dusted for today. Dont forget to keep an eye on the sky this afternoon, and maybe plant a tree if you get the chance. We will catch you all again tomorrow. Stay bright, Queensland, well see you next time on ParkSyde Bright Side.
